english_lines: This is a fighter's journey — his,
This is the prize he won by fighting,
You who laboured without rest — now,
Are you going to take rest?
You who laboured without rest — now,
Are you going to take rest?
You who crawled in your mother's lap,
Are you going to sleep beneath the ground?
notes: The repeated `ஓய்வில்லாமல்... / ஓய்வு கொள்ள...` contrast remains repeated rather than compressed.
Colloquial `போறியா` remains direct spoken questioning instead of being elevated into formal elegy.

english_lines: Little lion who came to awaken the youth,
Sprightly golden one who shone like a young sun,
The murder-mad weapons of caste division struck you,
They took the life you lived for principle,
You who laboured without rest — now,
Are you going to take rest?
notes: `குட்டிச்சிங்கம்` remains the intimate political image `little lion`; `சுட்டித்தங்கம்` is kept as `sprightly golden one` rather than generalized praise.
`கொலைவெறி ஜாதிபேத ஆயுதங்கள்` remains a direct chain of murder-fury, caste division and weapons; the political accusation is not softened.

source_tamil_lines: இயேசு புத்தர் நபிகள் காந்தி காட்டும் வழியிலே
பேசும் புயல் பெரியார் அண்ணா அம்பேத்கர் மொழியிலே
குன்றம் போல முழங்கி நடந்த குலவிளக்கு நீதியா
உன் கொடி நிழலில் என்றும் நாங்கள் கூடுவோம் பாரடா
english_lines: On the path shown by Jesus, Buddha, the Prophets and Gandhi,
In the words of the speaking storm — Periyar, Anna, Ambedkar,
O lamp of the lineage who walked roaring like a mountain — is this justice?
Under the shade of your flag, we will gather forever — see, da.
notes: The printed chain Jesus / Buddha / Prophets / Gandhi / Periyar / Anna / Ambedkar remains intact and in source order.
`பேசும் புயல்` remains `speaking storm`; `குலவிளக்கு` remains `lamp of the lineage` rather than being replaced by generic leader language.
The rough-intimate vocative force in `பாரடா` is retained with `da`.

translator_notes: The song is an elegy built from political kinship, martyrdom and colloquial address. The English keeps the grief and ideological naming explicit.
This is a literary source-faithful translation, not a singable adaptation.
